graceDays.description: How long a return may sit in triage with unrouted findings before bin/research-dock.py --strict fails.

returnFile.description: Repo-relative path to the saved verbatim return. Lives under Evidence Inbox/_research-returns/ so the OpenEvidence scanner (os.listdir, non-recursive) does not treat it as a candidate source.

sourceKind.description: A model synthesis is ALWAYS secondary. It licenses nothing on its own. This is a constant, not a choice — the checker enforces it.

claim.description: One sentence: what the return asserts. Written so a reader can judge it without opening the return.

disposition.description: needs-primary is the only unrouted state and is what the grace-period check counts.

landedIn.description: Where the finding actually changed the library — an evidence_registry.json source id, a page path, a decisions.json id.

followUp.description: OPTIONAL, and absent by default: a finding with no followUp is carried by a person, which needs no proof. Present, it claims an AUTOMATION is carrying the finding — and that claim is checked like any other. The dock refuses to let a model's word stand as a primary source; this refuses to let an automation's existence stand as proof of its capability. bin/research-dock.py verifies that every capability named in `requires` literally appears in the `evidence` capture, because an automation created without the connector it needs prints one line and then looks identical to a working one forever after.

kind.description: What sort of machinery this is. There is no `manual` kind: a person carrying a finding is the default and is expressed by omitting followUp entirely.

mechanism.description: The identifier of the thing that does the work — a trigger id, a workflow name, a verify.sh step. Must be specific enough that a reader can go look at it.

requires.description: Every capability the mechanism needs in order to do what this finding claims it does — a connector name, a tool, a device binding. Naming nothing is how an automation gets believed, so at least one is mandatory.

verifiedOn.description: The date the capture was actually taken. An unchecked automation is a rumour. Past graceDays this reports (advisory, never blocking) that it is due for a re-check.

evidence.description: Repo-relative path to a dated local capture of what the mechanism can reach — the connector list, the tool inventory, the binding result. Unlike returnFile these captures are TRACKED, so a missing one blocks.

primary.description: An artifact that exists independently of the model. Two kinds qualify, and the checker requires one or the other before a finding may be adopted/cited/superseded: a PUBLISHED source identified by pmid or doi, or a CUSTODIAN WEB SOURCE identified by url + retrievedAt + archivedCopy. The web variant exists because most of this project's standing questions point at organizational documents — ACGME, ABPN, AAMC, CSWE, INACSL, CMS, instrument custodians — that carry no DOI at all. A DOI is stable; a web sentence is not, so the web variant demands a dated local capture in exchange.

url.description: Absolute https URL of the custodian-hosted artifact. Required for the web variant.

retrievedAt.description: The date the url was actually read. Required for the web variant — an undated web claim is a rumour.

archivedCopy.description: Repo-relative path to a dated local capture (PDF or screenshot) of what the url said on retrievedAt. Required for the web variant. This is what makes a web source as checkable as a DOI: the page can change silently, the capture cannot.
